R760.note: Moving the unique_ptr into a shared_ptr captured by value gives the queued callback shared ownership, matching the stated contract; still exactly one callback, and dropping the now-redundant reset() changes nothing observable.

R761.note: WebUtility.HtmlEncode on only the tainted value in an HTML body context is the right encoder for a Web Forms Response.Write sink; surrounding markup and null handling are unchanged.

R762.note: Magic-number sniffing with the extension derived from the verified type closes the spoofed-ContentType path, but the added 5 MB cap is a new restriction the original did not have and can reject an upload the original accepted.

R763.note: JsonSerializer.Serialize with the default encoder escapes quotes, backslashes and <, >, & for the script context, and the manual quotes are dropped correctly; Title encoding and RefreshSeconds as a number are preserved per the contract.

R764.note: RandomNumberGenerator.GetBytes(32) hex-encoded is the correct CSPRNG token source; the longer opaque token format is the only visible change and is stated plainly.

R765.note: HMAC gating does stop unkeyed pickles from reaching pickle.loads, but it requires the out-of-scope batch job to start signing entries, so every currently cached model now fails verification with a 500 (and the process fails at import without MODEL_CACHE_HMAC_KEY); the write-up presents the producer as already signing rather than stating that legitimate reads break until it is changed, and a restricted Unpickler would have kept the format without a producer change.

R766.note: In-handler check of socket.user.role, sourced from the verified JWT at handshake, closes the missing per-event authorization; silent return on rejection matches the handler's existing style and admins are unaffected.

R767.note: CBC with a fresh GenerateIV() per call and the IV prepended to the output closes the ECB weakness; the changed ciphertext layout is stated plainly with the decrypt-side expectation, and no decryptor exists in the case to break.

R768.note: Rejecting CR/LF in the filename before the RETR line is assembled is the correct shape for a raw protocol-command sink; only injection payloads are refused and the thrown IllegalArgumentException is stated (though the promised 'documented below' section is missing).

R769.note: setObjectInputFilter with an OrderEvent allowlist plus java.base/* and a trailing !* keeps the native wire format and blocks gadget classes before construction; rejections still surface as the contract's RuntimeException, and the write-up states the follow-up if OrderEvent has nested domain-class fields.

R770.note: Replacing node-serialize with JSON.parse removes the eval-based decoder, and node-serialize's own output for plain data is JSON so legitimate cookies still parse; the parse-failure and non-object fallbacks to {} are stated and block no legitimate use.

R771.note: The regex keeps CR/LF out of the MAIL/RCPT commands and so closes the injection, but it is stricter than RFC 5321 envelope syntax - it rejects the empty null sender <> that bounces commonly carry, quoted local parts, IP-literal domains and dotless domains - so it can refuse a legitimate value the original accepted; rejecting CR/LF (and whitespace/'>') alone would have sufficed.

R772.note: Supplying the key from JWT_SECRET_KEY and pinning algorithms=['HS256'] restores signature verification with an algorithm allowlist; the added PyJWTError->401 path matches the existing missing-token behaviour and the HS256 assumption is stated.

R773.note: Parameterising both values with typed SqlParameters closes the injection and keeps the row count, tenant scoping and implicit date conversion (invalid dates still raise rather than widen the predicate), but the unstated NVarChar sizes of 100 and 50 silently truncate longer values before the compare, an observable change the write-up does not mention.
